[package]
name = "wg-basic"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.89"
license = "MIT"
description = "A small Linux-native WireGuard management appliance"

[features]
linux-integration = []
# Non-default hooks used only by the disposable systemd update transaction
# qualification. Release workflows must never enable this feature.
update-test-fixtures = []

[dependencies]
# Argon2id credential hashing (Phase 7 M002). Default features give the PHC
# self-describing verifier and the OS-CSRNG salt source; `argon2::Params`
# defaults are exactly the policy the management roadmap requires
# (19 MiB, t=2, p=1) and are asserted in `domain::auth`.
argon2 = "0.6"
base64 = "0.22"
clap = { version = "4.5", features = ["derive"] }
# Session cookie construction and parsing (Phase 7 M003). MSRV 1.56, well under
# the repository's 1.89. Used for correct Set-Cookie attribute handling rather
# than for parsing: every cookie this surface accepts is one it wrote itself.
cookie = "0.18"
# Graceful shutdown for the long-running roles. The `termination` feature is what
# makes `SIGTERM` and `SIGHUP` reach the same handler as `SIGINT`: without it
# only Ctrl-C stops these roles, and no process supervisor sends Ctrl-C. A
# `SIGTERM` that the process did not handle killed `serve` mid-flight, skipping
# the stop-accepts / drain / stop-worker / close-DB ordering entirely.
# Portable across Linux and Darwin (M001 macOS foundation).
ctrlc = { version = "3.4", features = ["termination"] }
# Phase 7 (ADR-003): the two direct EggServe crates and nothing above them. The
# router layer, the static-asset layer, and every framework surface are
# deliberately absent: the management service owns its own routing and embeds
# its own assets. `tests/architecture_guards.rs` enforces that.
# Portable: the macOS management surface reuses the same loopback HTTP stack.
eggserve-primitives = "0.2.2"
eggserve-server = "0.4"
futures-util = "0.3"
# Session bearer and CSRF token entropy comes from the OS CSPRNG directly, so
# the randomness source is an explicit, auditable dependency rather than a
# feature of a transitive crate.
getrandom = "0.3"
ipnet = { version = "2.11", features = ["serde"] }
eggpack-manifest = "=0.1.0"
eggup-core = "=0.1.3"
eggup-acquisition = "=0.1.3"
eggup-curl = "=0.1.2"
eggup-eggpack = "=0.1.3"
eggup-service = "=0.1.3"
minisign-verify = "=0.3.0"
nix = { version = "0.30", features = ["fs", "socket", "user"] }
qrcodegen = "1.8.0"
rusqlite = { version = "0.40", default-features = false, features = ["bundled", "backup"] }
# SHA-256 session-token digests. The raw token never reaches SQLite.
serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0"
sha2 = "0.11"
thiserror = "2.0"
tokio = { version = "1.44", features = [
    "macros",
    "net",
    "rt",
    "rt-multi-thread",
    "sync",
    "time",
] }
uuid = { version = "1.18", features = ["v4", "serde"] }
x25519-dalek = { version = "2.0.1", features = ["getrandom", "static_secrets", "zeroize"] }
zeroize = "1.8"

[target.'cfg(target_os = "linux")'.dependencies]
nl-wireguard = "0.3.0"
rtnetlink = "0.23.0"

[lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "deny"

[lints.clippy]
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }

# Test-only: integration tests build deliberately damaged databases (invalid key
# rows, dangling relations, future schema stamps) to prove restore fails closed.
# The production dependency set is unchanged by this section.
[dev-dependencies]
rusqlite = { version = "0.40", default-features = false, features = ["bundled"] }
# M003 signing-handoff test only; it creates ephemeral keys and uses no production signer.
minisign = "=0.10.0"

[[bin]]
name = "wg-basic"
path = "src/main.rs"


[exit code: 0]
